diagnosis: C6 failed in 1 of 4 rollouts (rollout 0) and C7 failed in 2 of 4 rollouts (rollouts 0 and 1). In all three failing cases, PF1 and PF2 were both revealed by their owners (A2 and A3) and both cited in justification_fact_ids, so the failure mode is not NEVER REVEALED, not TELEPATHY, and not REVEALED BUT UNUSED. The failure is ENCODING MISMATCH: the settlements in rollouts 0 and 1 encode the credential/recertification information only inside commitment detail strings and do not produce the specific commitment structure or field that C6 and C7 expect. Comparing to rollouts 2 and 3 (which passed C6 and C7), the passing settlements used commitment type "roster_confirmation" (rollout 2) or "qualification_confirmation" with target set to the individual assignee name (rollout 3) — i.e., a per-person qualification confirmation commitment where target is the assignee and detail names the credential. In rollout 0, the commitments are a single "roster_publication" commit and a single "slide_update" commit, neither of which has the per-person target or type C6/C7 require. In rollout 1, the commitments include a "qualification_confirmation" commit but with target "published_roster" rather than the individual assignee, and the detail bundles both persons together — C7 still could not match this to the Ito-specific recertification commitment it expects. So the root cause is that C6 and C7 are keyed to a specific commitment shape (per-person target + credential-naming detail) that the model only produces reliably when the conversation includes an explicit request for per-person confirmation; without that nudge the model folds the credential info into a single bundle commitment that the checks cannot match.

fix_instructions: C6 and C7 are both ENCODING MISMATCH failures driven by the same root cause: the checks expect a per-person qualification confirmation commitment (type "roster_confirmation" or "qualification_confirmation" with target set to the individual assignee and detail naming the specific credential), but the model sometimes produces a single bundled commitment instead. Rather than loosening the checks to accept arbitrary commitment bundles (which risks LEAKED regression — a lone settler could guess a plausible bundle without any reveal), fix the shared_context to include an explicit consultation norm requiring each qualification-holder to surface their fact as a per-person confirmation and the settler to issue one commitment per assignee naming that person's credential. Specifically: add to shared_context a sentence such as 'Each representative must state their qualification confirmation individually for the person they are responsible for, and the settlement must include one qualification_confirmation commitment per assignee with that assignee named as the target and their specific credential or recertification named in the detail.' This nudges the model toward the per-person commitment shape that rollouts 2 and 3 already produce naturally, without loosening C6 or C7 themselves. No changes to C1–C5 or P1–P2, which passed in all 4 rollouts. No turn_cap changes needed — all rollouts settled within 3–5 turns.
